Build observation windows from alpha shapes of high-density regions

Source: R/preprocess.R
alpha_windows.Rd

Builds closed observation windows from alpha shapes of high-density cell regions. Separated regions are kept apart, and each is returned as its own owin object, sorted by area from largest to smallest.

Usage

alpha_windows(image_kde, alpha = 200, cutoff = 0.002, fill_holes = TRUE)

Arguments

image_kde

Output of kde_est.

alpha

Positive number controlling how tightly the window follows the shape of the high-density cell region, in the same units as the coordinates. Smaller values give a tighter, more detailed boundary and may split the region into several pieces; larger values give a smoother boundary that bridges small gaps. As a rough guide, empty gaps wider than about 2 * alpha separate regions or form holes. Default is 200.

cutoff

Density threshold used to remove low-density areas. Default is 0.002.

fill_holes

Logical. If TRUE (default), holes within each region are filled, so each window is bounded by its outer boundary only. If FALSE, holes are kept and excluded from the window.

Value

A named list of owin objects (region1, region2, ...).

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
data(example_image)
wins <- alpha_windows(kde_est(example_image))
wins <- alpha_windows(kde_est(example_image), alpha = 100, cutoff = 2e-3, fill_holes = FALSE)
plot(wins$region1)} # }
